parts.gloss: if hands are folded (cease to work)

words.gloss: if hands are folded (cease to work)

literal: If the ploughmen's hands are folded, there is no stability of existence even for those who say we have renounced all that is desired.
translation: If the hands of ploughmen are folded in idleness, there is no stability of life even for those who claim to have renounced all worldly desires.
modern: உழவர்களுடைய கைகள் வேலை செய்யாமல் முடங்கிப் போனால், 'நாங்கள் ஆசைகளைத் துறந்துவிட்டோம்' என்று கூறும் துறவிகளுக்கும் கூட இவ்வுலகில் வாழ வழியில்லாமல் போகும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes that agriculture is the ultimate support for every member of society, including those who have withdrawn from worldly life. The phrase 'கைம்மடங்கின்' metaphorically describes farmers stopping their work, while 'விட்டேம் என்பார்' refers to ascetics who have renounced all desires. Even though these ascetics have given up material wants, they still require food to sustain their physical existence. Without the active labor of the ploughmen, even the most detached spiritual seekers cannot survive, proving that all human existence relies on the farmer.
